newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy bad loans equalled 11 pct of loans in August.
newsitem.headline: Italy bad loans equalled 11 pct of loans in August.

text.p: Italian banks' gross bad loans rose 15.2 percent in August year-on-year to reach 118.37 trillion lire, equal to 11.14 percent of total loans, the Italian Banking Association ABI said.
ABI said in its latest monthly report that the growth in bad loans had slowed down from July when they rose 15.4 percent year-on-year and from 15.8 percent in June.
The ratio of bad loans to all loans, however, continued to rise after 10.89 percent in July and 10.88 percent in June.

Turning to bank loan data for October, ABI said loans by banks holding short-term deposits, accounting for all high street banks, rose by just 4.08 percent year-on-year in the month to 861.0 trillion lire, down from an increase of 4.21 percent in September.
In August, loans rose 3.87 percent year-on-year.
Lira loans rose 6.49 percent in October to 785.0 trillion lire after a 6.65 percent rise in September.
But foreign currency loans fell 15.64 percent to 76.0 trillion lire after a drop of 15.16 percent in September.
High street bank deposits rose just 4.22 percent year-on-year in October to 865.0 trillion lire against an increase of 4.74 percent in September and of 4.78 percent in August.
